PRMT5 expression and activity (H4R3me2s) were elevated in all 5 ANNUBP samples with MTAP loss, indicating compensatory PRMT5 dependency in this NF1-associated premalignant stage.

PRMT5 is upregulated with MTAP loss in NF1-associated and sporadic MPNST; genetic/chemical PRMT5 inhibition selectively impaired MTAP-deficient MPNST cell growth via DNA damage and G2/M arrest, synergizing with chemotherapy.
PROS1 is expressed by stromal, immune, and some Schwann cells; CellPhoneDB predicts PROS1 signals via AXL to SCP-like cells, other SC types, and stromal/immune cells in PN.
PTEN, a tumor suppressor regulating PI3K/AKT/TOR, is significantly downregulated in MPNST vs neurofibroma and proposed as a biomarker for TOR-inhibitor efficacy.

SHP2 inhibition (SHP099) lowers RAS-GTP, blocks RAF/MEK/ERK signaling, suppresses MPNST cell growth and tumor volume, extends survival in allograft and PDX models; combination with hydroxychloroquine prevents/delays resistance.
SHP2 (PTPN11) inhibitor SHP099, combined with MEK inhibitor, reduced RAS-MAPK signaling upstream of RAS, restored chondrogenic fate, and prevented tibial pseudarthrosis in Nf1-deficient mice.
PTPRS downregulated in PNF tissue, suppresses EMT/migration by inhibiting EGFR expression/phosphorylation; low PTPRS correlates with recurrence
RABL6A is an oncogenic GTPase essential for MPNST progression, inactivating RB1 by hyperactivating CDKs (via p27 loss) and activating MEK/Myc, sensitizing cells to CDK4/6 inhibitors.
MEKi decreases RAD51 transcription/foci in NF1-deficient glioblastoma, creating HR-deficient state that sensitizes tumors to radiation-induced DNA damage.
RAD51-mediated homologous recombination repairs radiation-induced DNA double-strand breaks in VS cells; RAD51 inhibitor RI-1 blocks repair, enhancing radiation-induced cell death.
HuR binds CCND1, CCND2, CDK2, CDK6, p27, E2F1, E2F2, E2F3 mRNAs; HuR silencing reduces cyclin/CDK/E2F protein levels and E2F-driven signatures, driving G1 cell cycle arrest in MPNST cells.

RB1 tumor suppressor is inactivated by RABL6A-driven CDK hyperactivation in MPNSTs; reactivating RB1 via CDK4/6 inhibition is proposed as therapeutic strategy, though RB1 remains genetically wild-type.
RECQL4 knockdown in NF1-associated MPNST cell lines (NF90-8, ST88-14) increased apoptosis and sensitized cells to ATR inhibitors; NF1-MPNST tissue showed lower RECQL4 expression.
RNF213 p.R4810K variant confirmed in Japanese NF-1 patients with moyamoya syndrome, consistent with its role as MMD/MMS susceptibility variant.
RRM2 overexpressed in NF1-associated MPNST, correlates with poor survival; knockdown/inhibition reduced proliferation and tumor growth in vitro and in vivo
SHH pathway genes (SHH, SMO, GLI1) and reduced PTCH1 are transcriptionally activated/derepressed in PRC2-deficient NF1-mutant iHSCs, linking SHH activation to MPNST pathogenesis subgroup.

Germline SMARCB1 inactivation plus loss of chromosome 22 and somatic NF2 mutation (four-hit model) drives SWN schwannomas; SMARCB1 germline mutations also predispose to rhabdoid tumors; INI1 loss aids diagnosis.

Pharmacologic SOS1 inhibition shows limited biochemical efficacy alone in iPN and pNF/MPNST lines; efficacy is significantly improved when SOS2 is co-repressed via CRISPRi, indicating SOS2 compensation limits SOS1 blockade.

Sox10-CreERT2-driven Nf1 biallelic inactivation in SOX10+ Schwann lineage cells generated nodular/discrete cNFs recapitulating human cutaneous neurofibromas; SOX10+ cells identified as cells of origin.
NF1-null SOX10+/HOXb7+ hiPSC-SCPs implanted in sciatic nerve formed pNFs; Sox10-CreERT2 Nf1fl/fl mice developed pNFs, establishing SOX10+ cells as tumor-initiating cells.
SPP1 expression rises with tumor severity; SPP1 highly expressed in a distinct macrophage subset (MAC-3) dominant sender in MPNST; Spp1 knockout extends survival in cisNf1+/-;Trp53+/- MPNST mice.

SPP1 initiated autocrine by SCP-like tumor cells in pNF; pre-tumor DhhCre;Nf1-/- DRG shows elevated Spp1 in Nes+ SCL cells versus control, an early tumorigenic event; confirmed spatially with CD44/NES/ERBB3 co-localization.
Src family kinase activation identified in NF2-null meningioma cells; dasatinib inhibits Src/SFK, tested alone and combined with mTORC1/2 inhibitor for growth inhibition

FLLL32 (JAK2/STAT3 inhibitor) reduced neurofibroma volume, suppressed macrophage and Schwann cell proliferation, lowered macrophage numbers, and decreased chemokines (Ccl2, Ccl6, Ccl12, Ccl22) in mouse neurofibromas.
Survivin overexpressed in VS tissue; lapatinib downregulated survivin in schwannoma cells, proposed as EGFR/ErbB2-regulated therapeutic target.
Low-dose simvastatin reduced aneurysm incidence, size, MMP-9 activation and ROS production in AngII-infused Nf1+/- mice via anti-inflammatory/antioxidant effects.
Pan-TEAD auto-palmitoylation inhibitors (VT1/VT2/VT3) significantly inhibit proliferation of human NF2-null meningioma cells and cell lines in vitro.

TEAD auto-palmitoylation inhibitors VT1/VT2 block proliferation and cause regression (shrinkage) plus increased apoptosis of vestibular schwannoma tumours in NF2-null mice in vivo, and reduce human schwannoma cell proliferation.
TEAD1 expression and promoter binding were suppressed after combined treatment, downregulating TUBA1B, KIF18A, TAZ, YAP, TP53, SP1 transcription, driving MPNST cell death.

Conditional TGFβ1 overexpression in Nf1-deficient Schwann cells (Hoxb7-Cre) increased PNF burden, DRG volume, decreased survival, and drove malignant transformation to MPNST in vivo, with elevated BM proteins.

Nf1-deficient Schwann cells secrete Tgfb1, driving pSMAD2 activation and fibrotic differentiation of SSPCs; TGFβ blocking antibody reduced fibrosis and restored bone union in mutant mice.
YAP activation upregulates TGF-β1 secretion from cNF cells, synergizing with CCL5 to promote macrophage recruitment and proliferation, elevated in patient cNF tissue.

PRG-N-01 directly binds the TβR1 kinase domain (aa230-322), blocking aberrant TβR1-RKIP interaction without affecting canonical TGF-β signaling, thereby preventing RKIP degradation and suppressing DRG schwannoma growth.
Galunisertib (TGFβRI inhibitor) reduced PNF number, tumor diameter, tumor burden index, collagen, and basement membrane proteins (LAMB1, NID1, LAMC) in Nf1 mutant mice.
TGFβ1R knockdown/overexpression in THP-1 macrophages altered p21/p27/PCNA and cell cycle progression, demonstrating TGF-β1/TGFβR signaling drives macrophage proliferation in cNF.
Fimepinostat upregulates TRAIL R2 protein and transcript, contributing to caspase-3-dependent apoptosis, in schwannoma model cells including NCH1 spinal (non-vestibular) cells.
Fimepinostat upregulates TRAIL R2 protein and gene expression in HS02/HS05 and patient-derived vestibular schwannoma cells, contributing to caspase-3-dependent apoptosis.
Fimepinostat downregulates TNFR1 protein (Western blot) and gene expression (RT-qPCR) by 16h treatment in schwannoma model cells including NCH1 (non-vestibular).

VEGF stimulation transiently suppresses neurofibromin expression, correlating with Erk/Akt activation and enhanced endothelial proliferation, network formation, and retinal neovascularization in Nf1-deficient models.

VEGFR2 inhibition by cabozantinib linked to reduced neoangiogenesis (CD31+ vessels) in PN tumors, supporting anti-tumor mechanism.

Murine forward genetic screen and human tissue microarrays showed canonical Wnt activation transforms Schwann cells; Wnt downregulation reduced tumorigenic phenotype of MPNST cell lines.
Merlin loss activates Wnt/β-catenin via CBP-β-catenin/FOXM1 axis promoting meningioma growth; ICG-001 disrupts CBP-β-catenin interaction, reducing tumor growth in vitro and PDX.

Merlin deficiency in meningioma cells increases YAP expression and nuclear localization, driving proliferation; YAP knockdown alleviates merlin-deficient proliferation, and low-merlin regions of NF2-positive meningiomas show more nuclear YAP.
Fimepinostat reduces YAP levels in HS02/HS05 cells and NCH1 spinal (non-vestibular) schwannoma model, implicated in cell death signaling downstream of merlin loss.
YAP, a Hippo pathway effector, is upregulated in cNF tissue and Nf1-ablated cells; activation drives tumor cell proliferation and macrophage accumulation via CCL5/TGF-β1.
HuR binds YAP1, TEAD1, TEAD2 mRNAs; HuR silencing reduces YAP/TAZ pathway protein levels and downstream target gene expression, anticorrelating with YAP/TAZ hyperactivation signatures in MPNST cells.
YAP/TAZ knockdown reduces proliferation of NF2-null BenMen-1 meningioma cells; TAZ drives ALDH1A1 expression, showing YAP/TAZ act as growth drivers in meningioma cells.

Case report: imatinib (a KIT inhibitor, used for patient's c-Kit-expressing GIST) slightly reduced new c-NF development but increased size of pre-existing c-NFs; KIT involvement in c-NFs is speculative, not directly measured.

Selumetinib (MEK1/2 inhibitor) is approved for NF1 pNFs; sgNF1 iPNs show decreased pERK sensitivity/altered pMEK feedback vs controls. No endothelial cells, retinal neovascularization, or Ras-Akt vascular mechanism appear anywhere in this paper.

EED/PRC2 loss impairs Schwann cell proliferation and delays axon regeneration after nerve injury in mouse Eed cKO; MPNST link is discussion-based, citing prior literature that PRC2 loss co-occurs with NF1/CDKN2A/TP53 alterations in human MPNSTs, not directly tested in this study's model.
Review states neurofibromin downregulates Ras signaling generally; no MPNST-specific RAS mechanism or manifestation data provided for this target-disease pair.

Paper reports germline LZTR1 mutations in 24.4% (41/168) of sporadic schwannomatosis patients, uniformly distributed across domains; cites 24 SMARCB1-negative schwannomatosis families with LZTR1 variants; invokes two-hit hypothesis.

This paper's own MPNST cell-line data show MAP3K8 gained rhythmic expression only in S462; MAPK pathway's role in NF1 circadian regulation is cited from prior animal/Drosophila studies, not directly tested here.

Paper shows human NF2 protein forms solid-like condensates requiring PI4P binding and PTPN14 promotes NF2 medial apical localization in MDCK cells; no schwannoma, hearing loss, or vestibular phenotype studied.
SMARCB1 variants cause a schwannomatosis subset with increased malignancy/MPNST risk; the paper attributes prominent pain and unilateral vestibular schwannoma risk specifically to LZTR1, not SMARCB1.
BMPR2 p.M365I variant from NF-1 patient showed partial loss of BMP4-induced luciferase activity, cell-surface expression preserved; PAH-gene modifier of moyamoya syndrome.

FAK/p-FAK were quantified by immunoblot in IOMM-Lee malignant meningioma cells; FAK significantly decreased at high glucose+MGO, p-FAK decreased with MGO at low and high glucose. Used as readout, not a therapeutic target.
SOX10 silencing via chromatin closure occurs in 3KO NC model representing early MPNST-like stage; ANNUBP samples show high SOX10 expression in glial component, not silencing.

Angiogenesis via VEGF contributes to LGG growth; anti-VEGF antibody bevacizumab produces rapid radiological response and visual improvement in progressive OPG, but high relapse rate after discontinuation.

ATR inhibitors (AZD6738, VE-821) reduced survival in glioma cells (U251), with RECQL4-knockdown cells showing greater sensitivity than controls.

RECQL4 knockdown in U251 glioma cells increased apoptosis and susceptibility to ATR inhibitors; RECQL4 expression higher in HGG generally.
pSrc/SFK (Y416) phosphorylation is elevated in primary human VS tumors and mouse allograft tumors and reduced by dasatinib treatment, independent of mTORC1/2 signaling.
SGK1 (mTORC2 target) is constitutively activated with NF2 loss in meningioma, cited from prior work; this paper's own new data on SGK1 activation is in NF2-null Schwann cells/VS, not meningioma.

TGFBR3 expression elevated in NF1 fibroblasts and plasma, decreased in ataluren-responsive cells; proposed as monitoring biomarker, not a therapeutic target.
